message.content:
# Finding ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Method: Integration by Parts (twice)

**First integration by parts:**

Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = exp(x)*cos(x) + \int exp(x)*sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (on the remaining integral):

Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int exp(x)*sin(x)\, dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - \int exp(x)*cos(x)\, dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - I$$

**Combining results:**

$$I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I$$

$$2*I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{exp(x)*cos(x)}{2} + \frac{exp(x)*sin(x)}{2} + C$$

## Verification (differentiate):

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{exp(x)*cos(x)}{2} + \frac{exp(x)*sin(x)}{2}\right] = \frac{exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*sin(x)}{2} + \frac{exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)}{2} = exp(x)*cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*cos(x)/2 + exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C</answer>
